subtitle: When Budshah Turned Workmen into Weavers of Wealth and Memory

panels.shot: towering interior wide of a royal workshop opening into river and mountains beyond
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin stands at the threshold of a vast karkhana, watching rows of artisans at looms and paper vats as the Jhelum river gleams beyond and the snow peaks rise under a pale sky.

dialogue.text: In Budshah Zain-ul-Abidin’s time, paper from rags, painted pen cases and coded carpets turned Kashmir’s workshops into engines of memory, beauty and coin.

i18n.hi: बदशाह ज़ैनुल आबिदीन के ज़माने में चिथों का कागज़, रंगीन कलमदान और कोड वाली कालीनों ने कश्मीर के कारखानों को याद, ख़ूबसूरती और सिक्के की इंजन बना दिया।

panels.shot: slow push-in from birch forest to palace study
panels.action: In a grove of tall birch trees, a worker peels bark while, dissolved in the same frame, Zain-ul-Abidin sits in his palace study, unrolling a brittle birch-bark manuscript with care.

dialogue.text: For centuries Kashmir wrote on birch bark from the forest. In Budshah’s court, the bark began to crack under the growing weight of books, accounts and decrees.

i18n.hi: सदियों तक कश्मीर जंगलों की भूर्ज छाल पर लिखता रहा। बदशाह के दरबार में किताबों, हिसाबों और फ़रमानों का बोझ बढ़ा, तो छाल भरभराने लगी।

panels.shot: medium interior of court with scribes and scholars around the Sultan
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin sits on a low throne in the audience hall, surrounded by scribes with reed pens and scholars holding manuscripts, as a tray of worn birch-bark leaves lies open before him.

dialogue.text: Srivara’s Jaina-Rajatarangini shows Budshah surrounded by poets, historians and clerks. A kingdom of words needed a better skin to carry its memory.

i18n.hi: श्रीवर की जैना-राजतरंगिणी में बदशाह शायरों, मुंसियों और इतिहासकारों से घिरा है। लफ़्ज़ों की रियासत को अपनी याद के लिए बेहतर क़लमचा चाहिए था।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of karkhana courtyard by the Jhelum
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin walks through a riverside courtyard where laborers bring bundles of old cloth and ropes, while craftsmen prepare vats and wooden frames under the open sky.

dialogue.text: G.M.D. Sufi and Bamzai note a new royal karkhana for paper. Rags and ropes, once waste, began their second life as the kingdom’s pages.

i18n.hi: जी.एम.डी. सूफ़ी और बमज़ाई एक नए शाही कागज़ी कारख़ाने का ज़िक्र करते हैं। चिथड़े और रस्सियाँ, जो पहले कचरा थे, अब बादशाहत के सफ़ों में दूसरा जनम लेते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on hands at a paper vat, with Budshah observing in background
panels.action: A craftsman’s hands stir a slurry of rag pulp in a wooden vat, lifting a mesh frame as a thin sheet settles, while Zain-ul-Abidin watches intently from behind.

dialogue.text: Under Budshah’s patronage, rag paper making was organised and scaled. The process itself came from wider Iranian-Central Asian currents already flowing through Kashmir.

i18n.hi: बदशाह की सरपरस्ती में चीथड़ा-कागज़ बनाना बाक़ायदा संगठित और बड़ा किया गया। तरीक़ा ईरान–मध्य एशिया की वही लहरों से आया जो पहले ही कश्मीर से गुज़र रही थीं।

panels.shot: interior wide of royal scriptorium lined with fresh paper sheets
panels.action: Inside a bright scriptorium, fresh sheets of rag paper dry on cords, while scribes sit cross-legged, copying texts, and Zain-ul-Abidin stands at the doorway with a quiet smile.

dialogue.text: With rag paper, birch bark became less central. Manuscripts multiplied, accounts thickened, and the Sultan’s orders travelled faster on durable leaves.

i18n.hi: चीथड़ा-कागज़ आने पर भूर्ज छाल का रुतबा घटा। मुरक़े बढ़े, हिसाब मोटे हुए, और सुल्तान के हुक्म मज़बूत पन्नों पर दूर तक दौड़ने लगे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Budshah at his desk with ornate pen case
panels.action: Zain-ul-Abidin sits at a low writing desk, his hand resting near a plain wooden pen case, while across from him an artisan presents a richly painted, lacquered pen case.

dialogue.text: Where there is paper and ink, there is the qalam. Around the pen grew a new art in Budshah’s karkhanas—the making of decorated qalamdan, pen cases.

i18n.hi: जहाँ कागज़ और स्याही, वहाँ क़लम। क़लम के इर्द-गिर्द बदशाह के कारख़ानों में नई फ़नकारी उगी—सजे-सजाए क़लमदान, कलमदानों की बनावट।

panels.shot: close-up of a papier-mache pen case being painted
panels.action: A craftsman’s steady hand paints delicate floral and geometric motifs on a smooth papier-mache pen case, with other unfinished forms stacked nearby and Zain-ul-Abidin’s silhouette faint in the background.

dialogue.text: M.Y. Saraf and Kashir’s historians trace kar-i-qalamdan—papier-mache pen-case work—to this era, when royal patronage turned small painted objects into a formal, court-linked craft.

i18n.hi: एम.वाई. सराफ़ और ‘कशीर’ के इतिहासकार कर-ए-क़लमदान यानी पेपियर-माशे कलमदानकारी को इसी दौर से जोड़ते हैं, जब शाही सरपरस्ती ने छोटे रंगीन सामानों को दरबारी पेशा बना दिया।

panels.shot: wide of Naushahr street with karkhanas and merchants
panels.action: In Naushahr’s busy quarter near Srinagar, artisans carry trays of finished pen cases from a workshop as merchants examine them, while Zain-ul-Abidin rides past on horseback, observing the activity.

dialogue.text: These delicate cases, born in court karkhanas, travelled into Naushahr’s bazaars and beyond. Ornament fed prestige, and prestige fed trade.

i18n.hi: ये नाज़ुक डिब्बे, जो दरबार के कारख़ानों में जन्मे, नौशहर के बाज़ारों और बाहर तक पहुँचे। नक़्श से शान, और शान से सौदागरी बढ़ी।

panels.shot: interior wide of carpet workshop with looms and apprentices
panels.action: In a large hall, tall upright looms stand in rows. Men and boys sit before them, knotting wool, while Zain-ul-Abidin walks with a master weaver along the central aisle.

dialogue.text: Alongside paper and pen cases, Budshah’s karkhanas brought Persianate carpet weaving into a more ordered frame, drawing on skills already moving through trade and Sufi networks.

i18n.hi: कागज़ और कलमदान के साथ-साथ बदशाह के कारख़ानों ने फ़ारसी अन्दाज़ की कालीन बुनाई को ज़्यादा तरतीब दी, उन हुनरों को सँजोकर जो पहले ही सौदा और सूफ़ी सिलसिलों से चल रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot on a master weaver teaching an apprentice, Budshah watching
panels.action: A master weaver sits at a loom, guiding an apprentice’s hand to tie a knot on a partly woven carpet, while Zain-ul-Abidin stands behind them, his gaze fixed on the emerging pattern.

dialogue.text: Training was central. Under royal oversight, master weavers took on apprentices, turning scattered skill into a system of learning tied to the Sultan’s demand.

i18n.hi: तालीम सबसे अहम थी। शाही निगरानी में उस्ताद जुलाहों ने चेले लिए, बिखरी क़ाबिलियत को सुल्तान की माँग से बंधी सीख की नसों में बदला।

panels.shot: close-up of taleem pattern sheet next to loom
panels.action: Next to a loom, a taleem pattern sheet lies open, marked with lines and coded symbols, while a weaver glances at it and then at the coloured threads hanging in order.

dialogue.text: Saraf describes the taleem system—coded instructions for designs. Written patterns let carpets be reproduced and orders fulfilled across different workshops.

i18n.hi: सराफ़ तलीम तरीक़े का ज़िक्र करते हैं—डिज़ाइन के कोड लिखे हुए हुक्म। लिखे पैटर्न ने कालीनों को दोहराना और अलग कारख़ानों में ऑर्डर पूरा करना आसान कर दिया।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of multiple looms following one taleem
panels.action: From above, several looms in the karkhana show weavers knotting similar motifs while identical taleem sheets lie by each, and Zain-ul-Abidin’s figure moves between them like a supervising presence.

dialogue.text: With taleem, design became a language. A motif written in code could be read by weavers across the valley, binding distant hands to one pattern.

i18n.hi: तलीम से डिज़ाइन एक ज़बान बन गया। कोड में लिखी कोई बेल-बूटा पूरा वादी में जुलाहों द्वारा पढ़ी जा सकती थी, दूर-दूर के हाथों को एक ही नक़्श में जोड़ते हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot of finished carpets being inspected
panels.action: Rows of finished carpets with intricate central medallions and borders lie rolled and stacked in the workshop courtyard, as Zain-ul-Abidin and his officials inspect them beside scribes noting inventories.

dialogue.text: Bamzai and Sufi show these carpets tied to royal and export economies. Each roll was both floor and ledger—a surface of beauty and a unit of value.

i18n.hi: बमज़ाई और सूफ़ी बताते हैं कि ये कालीनें शाही और बाहरी बाज़ारों से बँधी थीं। हर रोल ज़मीन भी था, हिसाब भी—हुस्न की सतह और क़ीमत की इकाई।

panels.shot: medium shot of merchants loading carpets onto boats on the Jhelum
panels.action: On the banks of the Jhelum, merchants and porters load rolled carpets and bundles of paper onto wooden boats, while Zain-ul-Abidin watches from the steps, with the city rising behind him.

dialogue.text: From Srinagar’s karkhanas, paper, pen cases and carpets moved onto boats and caravan paths, carrying Kashmir’s work to courts and markets beyond its mountains.

i18n.hi: स्रीनगर के कारख़ानों से कागज़, कलमदान और कालीनें नावों और क़ाफ़िलों पर चढ़कर पहाड़ों के पार दूसरे दरबारों और बाज़ारों तक चल पड़ीं।

panels.shot: close-up of a worker’s hands tying a carpet roll with rope
panels.action: A worker’s rough hands tie a rope around a carpet roll, his face focused and calm, while in the blurred background Zain-ul-Abidin speaks with an officer about production.

dialogue.text: “Let the workmen’s skill be our kingdom’s strength,”

i18n.hi: “मज़दूरों का हुनर ही हमारे राज्य की ताक़त बने,”

dialogue.text: Budshah’s policies drew state and artisan together. His coin, their craft, and the river’s route linked humble labour to royal revenue.

i18n.hi: बदशाह की नीतियों ने हुकूमत और दस्तकार को साथ बाँधा। उसका सिक्का, उनका हुनर और दरिया का रास्ता, छोटी मेहनत को शाही महसूल से जोड़ने लगे।

panels.shot: soft-focus montage of manuscript, pen case and carpet
panels.action: A gentle montage shows a scribe writing on rag paper, a papier-mache pen case resting beside him, and beneath, a knotted carpet with classic Persianate motifs spreading across the floor.

dialogue.text: The crafts were distinct—paper, pen case, carpet—but under Budshah they touched: the pen wrote on new paper, the pen case held it, the carpet carried those lives at their feet.

i18n.hi: हुनर अलग-अलग थे—कागज़, कलमदान, कालीन—मगर बदशाह के दौर में वे छू गए: क़लम नए कागज़ पर लिखी, कलमदान ने उसे थामा, और कालीनों ने उन ज़िंदगियों को पैरों तले ढोया।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Budshah in an empty workshop at dusk
panels.action: At dusk, Zain-ul-Abidin stands alone in the quiet karkhana hall, empty looms and tables around him, as fading light streams in and dust motes hang in the air.

dialogue.text: Historians remind us: Budshah did not invent every craft. He formalised, scaled and tied them to court and commerce, turning scattered skills into a woven system.

i18n.hi: मौरीख़ीन याद दिलाते हैं: बदशाह ने हर हुनर नहीं बनाया; उसने उन्हें बाक़ायदा किया, बड़ा किया और दरबार व सौदा से बाँधा, बिखरे हुनर को बुनी हुई प्रणाली में बदला।

panels.shot: final wide shot of modern Kashmiri crafts dissolving into Budshah’s karkhana
panels.action: Modern Kashmiri paper, papier-mache objects and carpets lie in a shop, then subtly dissolve into the image of Zain-ul-Abidin’s bustling karkhana, bridging centuries in one frame.

dialogue.text: In every Kashmiri sheet, painted case and carpet knot today, there is a trace of Budshah’s age—when a Sultan saw that a civilisation can travel in a worker’s hands.

i18n.hi: आज हर कश्मीरी कागज़ की शीट, रंगीन कलमदान और कालीन की गिरह में बदशाह के ज़माने की हल्की सी छाप है—जब एक सुल्तान ने समझा कि तहज़ीब मज़दूर के हाथों में सफ़र कर सकती है।

title_i18n.en: Paper Pen Cases and Paradise Carpets
